meta.title: Get started — Kanso
meta.description: Run Kanso with Docker, walk through the setup wizard, and file the first ticket. The two variables that are the whole configuration, and the keys that do the work.
head.title: A running instance, and a ticket in it.
head.lead: Two things to configure, one wizard, and six keys. Everything else has a defensible default or is derived, and can be changed later from settings.
run.title: Run it against your own Postgres
run.body: One image — the front end, the API and a proxy that routes between them — on one origin. Kanso does not ship a database: a container that owns your data is a container you cannot restart without thinking about it.
run.two: Those two things — the URL it lives at and the database it writes to — are the whole configuration. Caddy obtains a certificate for that host on its own, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 alike.
run.compose: No database yet? docker/docker-compose.yml ships a postgres:16-alpine beside the image. Copy it, change KANSO_PUBLIC_URL and the password, then docker compose up -d.
run.note: The host in SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL is resolved from inside the container. On Compose it is the service name; for a Postgres running on this machine but outside Docker it is host.docker.internal. It is never localhost, which is the container itself.
dev.title: Or run it from source
dev.body: The repository's own docker-compose.yml is a different thing: it builds both applications from source and serves them on two ports, which is what the Playwright suite drives. Fill in OIDC credentials in .env, or set KANSO_AUTH_MODE=dev.
dev.api: The REST API, the WebSocket and the MCP endpoint
dev.health: Liveness, readiness and the database check
dev.apps: To run the applications outside Docker and keep only Postgres in it:
wizard.title: The setup wizard
wizard.body: The first launch opens a wizard rather than a login screen, because there is nobody to log in as yet. It has four steps and only the first is required.
wizard.account: The owner account. An email address and a password. This account can configure the instance; nothing else can.
wizard.notion: Notion. Optional, and reopenable. Connecting it is a page of its own — see Notion.
wizard.google: Google sign-in. Optional. An instance can run on passwords alone.
wizard.preferences: Preferences. Theme, accent, sidebar. Per person, not per instance.
wizard.skip: Every step after the account is skippable and reopenable from settings — , — so you can be filing tickets in under a minute and decide the rest later.
wizard.invite: Whoever comes next arrives through an invitation link the owner generates, and sees only the preferences step. Notion and Google are instance-wide, so a member has nothing to decide there and the steps are hidden rather than shown disabled.
first.title: The first team, and the first ticket
first.body: A ticket belongs to a team, so a team comes first — the sidebar creates one. From then on the keyboard is the interface, and the same keys work in the list, on the board and on the timeline.
first.digits: Your team's first six statuses, in its own order
first.shift: Pick a status by name, including a seventh
first.help: Every shortcut, as this account has them bound
first.number: The ticket gets a short identifier of its team's own — KAN-1, then KAN-2 — allocated inside the insert transaction from a counter on the team row. Two people pressing c at the same moment get 41 and 42: no gaps, no collisions.
